thread:
Maya: FYI — running the 30d hosted demand sim and saw ~18% upside probability for token volume next month. Committed GPU add doesn't kick until 2026-05-10. We need a short-term hedge plan.

Devon: Ugh. 18% is non-trivial. Can you paste the sim assumptions? is this just embed-heavy customers or steady chat uplift?

Maya: Mix — two large customers increasing batch embed jobs + a general uptick in chat tail-latency traffic. Assumptions: baseline 120 GPU-equivalent hours/day, 90th pct demand spike ~142 GEH/day (18%); committed reserved capacity arriving +40 GPUs on 2026-05-10.

Leo: Quick thought: we can 1) enable temporary burst instances in eu-west while we wait, 2) shift lower-priority background embed jobs to dedicated pools or pre-warm caches, 3) tighten batching thresholds for small requests. Cost tradeoffs?

Anya: Agreed. Also we should validate billing mapping — last month we had an unexplained 3% charge delta due to SKU tagging. If burst uses on-demand SKUs, that could blow the hedge. Pinged billing-bot to run a sku-mapping check. :eyes:

billing-bot: Automated check complete. Found two historical charge lines with mismapped sku: `cloud.gpu.v2` labeled as `reserved` instead of `on-demand` for 2026-03-12 to 2026-03-14. Estimated impact: $8.5k (0.9% of monthly infra). Recommend tagging cleanup and retroactive correction request.

Devon: Good catch. If we can reclaim that mis-tag amount, it lowers the net cost of short bursts. But still need capacity strategy. Maya — can you run a quick scenario: cost of 18% burst via on-demand vs activating a small committed top-up (if procurement can accelerate)?

Maya: Running numbers now. Two scenarios:

- On-demand burst (30 days rolling): ~+25% unit cost vs reserved -> incremental $45k/mo for the observed uplift.
- Accelerated committed 40 GPUs (annual term pro-rated): amortized incremental $12k/mo but requires procurement and contract amendment; earliest ETA 2026-05-03 if we push.

Maya: Also sim of routing fallback: if we route <=10% of traffic to dedicated pools (lower perf but cheaper), increment cost savings ~8k/mo, latency SLO impact small for non-interactive workloads.

Leo: Those numbers favor getting the committed top-up if procurement can shave a week. Anya — can platform ops prep a contract amendment template for +40 GPUs? If legal takes >5 days, bursts are the fallback.

Anya: I'll start the amendment draft and tag Legal. Quick ask — what's the minimum guaranteed term procurement needs? We might propose a 3-mo bridge term.

Maya: Procurement expects standard 12mo for committed pricing, but sales/legal have accepted short bridges before. If we do 3-mo bridge pricing, unit cost will be between reserved and on-demand (~+10% vs reserved). Still cheaper than on-demand for 30d.

Devon: Operational checklist: 1) pre-approve burst-capacity pool (eu-west, us-central) 2) pre-warm a few nodes to reduce cold-starts 3) add routing rule to send low-priority embed batches to dedicated pools 4) billing sku guardrails. Who owns 1/2/3/4?

Maya: I'll take 1+2 (infra side). Leo takes 3 (routing). Anya takes 4 (billing/legal loop).

sre-bot: Incident note: last time we enabled eu-west burst, we hit a networking MTU mismatch causing 12% error rate for ~45m. Recommend running canary with smaller traffic % and include `net-mtu-check` in pre-warm.

Leo: Good call. We'll canary with 5% traffic for 1h and monitor error-rate and p95 latencies. If green, ramp to 25% for background jobs.

Maya: Action plan + timeline:
- Today: submit procurement amendment request (Anya), start sku-tag correction (Anya + billing-bot), enable burst pool pre-warm (Maya).
- T+1 day: run 1h canary at 5% (Leo/Maya).
- T+2 days: if canary passes, route up to 25% background jobs to dedicated pools and monitor cost/latency.
- T+7 days: procurement follow-up, finalize whether to proceed with committed top-up.

Devon: Sounds good. Please keep the thread updated with canary results and any unexpected billing flags.

Anya: Started the amendment draft and notified Legal. Billing sku correction ticket created: #BILL-4287.

Maya: Canary scheduled for 2798642060 (in 60s). Will post results here.

Maya: Canary done — 5% traffic, 1h. No MTU issues this time. Error-rate stable, p95 +12ms for affected routes. Cost delta as expected. Moving to 25% background routing.

Leo: Ramping to 25% now. Monitoring.

Maya: 25% ramp stable after 30m. CPU/GPU saturation within tolerances. Estimated cost savings ~7.4k/mo vs full on-demand burst.

Devon: Nice. Keep procurement cadence — if contract can be accelerated to 05-03 we still prefer committed top-up. Otherwise we keep the routing hedge as primary mitigation.

Anya: Legal replied — can do a 3-mo bridge on accelerated approval. Procurement ETA 2026-05-02. Drafting final amendment.

Maya: Closing loop: current posture = routing hedge active (25% background), burst pool pre-warmed, procurement + legal pursuing 3-mo committed bridge. Will update if demand sim changes. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
